To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the power spectral density (PSD) of self noise can be accurately approximated as a function of the signal-to-noise power ratio (SNR); and (2) for realistic spectra of phase error affecting the timing wave, the tracking performance of non-data-aid feedforward timing recovery (NDAF) is superior to that of non-data- aided feedback timing recovery (NDBF).

, in digital timing recovery, self noise does not affect the performance of feedback timing recovery with an optimized predetection filtering, but affects the performance of feedforward timing recovery, and, despite self noise feedforward timing recovery performs better than feedback timing recovery.
, for signalto-noise ratio lower that 50 dB and phase noise spectra with a corner frequency of 100 Hz, self noise affects feedforward timing recovery more than feedback timing recovery.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for signal to noise ratios higher than about 50 dB, self noise can be neglected and feedback timing recovery with optimal predetection filter is the best timing recovery technique.

, if self noise can be neglected, feedback timing recovery is the best solution; if self noise cannot be neglected and the signal-to-noise is high enough, feedforward timing is preferable; if the signal-to-noiseratio is too low to allow for feedforward timing recovery, feedback timing recovery must be adopted.
non-data-aid feedforward timing recovery should be preferred over non-data-aid feedback timing recovery in the digital receivers of digital radio communication systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while feedback timing is more robust against noise and interference, feedforward timing is more robust to phase noise.

, in digital receivers, feedforward timing synchronization should be adopted in place of feedback timing synchronization, provided that the signal-to-noise is high enough and the phase noise affecting the signal to be tracked is low enough.

, for the case of non-data-aiding timing recovery in a digital receiver, the use of feedback timing recovery is not recommended, unless the phase noise affecting the input timing wave is negligible, i.e. lower than -50 dBc/Hz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the first time, the impact of self noise on feedforward timing recovery has been quantified and it has been shown that it does not degrade performance of feedforward timing recovery.
